import pandas as pd

# Read CSV
df = pd.read_csv("housing.csv")

required_cols = ["population", "households", "median_house_value"]
for col in required_cols:
    if col not in df.columns:
        raise KeyError(f"Required column '{col}' not found in CSV")

# Compute population density (population per household), avoid division by zero
df["population_density"] = df["population"] / df["households"].replace({0: pd.NA})
df = df.dropna(subset=["population_density", "median_house_value"])

# Calculate Pearson correlation between population_density and median_house_value
correlation = df["population_density"].corr(df["median_house_value"])

# Create quantile bins of population_density to examine trend
# Use qcut with up to 10 bins, allow dropping duplicate edges
try:
    df["density_bin"] = pd.qcut(df["population_density"], q=10, duplicates="drop")
except ValueError:
    # If qcut fails (e.g., not enough unique values), fall back to cut with 10 equal-width bins
    df["density_bin"] = pd.cut(df["population_density"], bins=10)

# Aggregate statistics by bin
binned_stats = (
    df.groupby("density_bin")
    .agg(
        count=("median_house_value", "size"),
        mean_population_density=("population_density", "mean"),
        mean_median_house_value=("median_house_value", "mean"),
        median_median_house_value=("median_house_value", "median"),
        std_median_house_value=("median_house_value", "std"),
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Prepare result: include overall correlation and the binned summary
result = {"correlation_population_density_median_house_value": correlation, "binned_stats": binned_stats}
